result.headline: Throttle command dropped to 0 at ~104 s with no event; ch[2] followed, aircraft lost altitude.
result.explanation: A control fault occurred at about t=104.1 s on the throttle/motor loop (ch[2]). Throttle fell from 66% to 0 and stayed there. The motor output followed it and the aircraft descended. The recording does not show who commanded the zero.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT propulsion.throttle was varying, then held 0 from t=104.121 s to the end of the recording (12.079 s, 31 samples)
evidence.shows: The throttle command went to zero and stayed there. It is the earliest actuator-loop change. No mode event explains it.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT actuator.output[ch[2]] was varying, then held 1100 from t=105.016 s to the end of the recording (11.295 s, 34 samples)
evidence.shows: The throttle channel went to its minimum about 0.9 s after the command and then froze.

evidence.quote: ROLE actuator.output[ch[2]] follows propulsion.throttle (correlation 0.973 over the recording): it serves that loop
evidence.shows: ch[2] is the throttle/propulsion channel, and it followed the command down. The cut originates upstream of the output.

evidence.quote: SHIFT vehicle.altitude[relative] changed level for good at t=106.891 s: median 50.292 before, 20.287 after m (29.5x its variation before)
evidence.shows: Altitude fell from about 50 m to about 20 m, starting after the throttle cut. This is an effect.

evidence.quote: SHIFT vehicle.attitude[pitch] followed its setpoint worse for good from t=103.856 s: typical |error| 0.918 before, 3.292 after deg (4.2x its variation before)
evidence.shows: Pitch tracking degraded at the time of the throttle excursion. The pitch setpoint went to about -25 deg during the descent.

checked.check: Sequence of departures from baseline, 99-108 s
checked.result: The order was velocity[x] (103.218), throttle (103.776, up to 66%), ch[2] (103.977), pitch (106.162), altitude (106.891). Velocity[x] left baseline first, so a speed change preceded the throttle ramp.
checked.about: Throttle cut is the earliest actuator-side change; altitude loss is downstream

checked.check: Window 99-112 s on throttle, ch[2], altitude, pitch
checked.result: Throttle was 66 at 103.776 and 0 at 104.562. ch[2] was 1612 at 103.567, 1484 at 104.324 and 1100 at 105.016, then held. Altitude began falling at 107.092.
checked.about: Command-side cut, with the output following

checked.result: Only two start-up warnings at t=0.712 (low voltage, sensor health). No failsafe or mode change near the throttle cut.
checked.about: Cause of the throttle cut is not recorded

checked.result: ch[2] and throttle are essentially unchanged at that time (throttle level_change_z 1.0). The SHIFT is a smeared step from the later drop. The larger changes are in the yaw and roll setpoints, a manoeuvre.

hypotheses.claim: The throttle command was set to 0 by a mode change, failsafe or operator input that was not recorded.
hypotheses.because: Throttle fell first, and ch[2] followed it. No event explains it, so the commander is unknown.

hypotheses.claim: The motor or ESC lost power or failed, and the controller's throttle fell in response.
hypotheses.because: The signals show the command falling before the output froze, so this is not shown. Motor-side telemetry is absent.

hypotheses.claim: Low battery or power sag triggered the throttle cut.
hypotheses.because: A low-voltage warning appeared at start-up only. No battery signal exists in this recording to test it.

hypotheses.claim: An aggressive roll/yaw manoeuvre (roll setpoint ~40 deg from 100.4 s) loaded the aircraft, and the fault became visible then.
